text:
The Flames lost Kevin Bahl for the season earlier this month, and the headlines since have mostly been about how they replace him. Bahl and Simon Nemec had been an even pair by chances; now the minutes go to depth that hasn't been tested. The bright spot on the blue line is Zayne Parekh, whose breakout has drawn headlines asking whether he is already one of the league's better defensemen.

The team around them is 10-12-2 and mostly earned it. Calgary has 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and allows about 3.5 goals a game. The power play creates little (0.39 expected goals a game), and Calgary takes more penalties than it draws. Matt Coronato (2 points in his last 10, 7.6 expected) and Joel Farabee (3 in 10, 8.0 expected) are both running cold on the Mikael Backlund line, which has been outscored 4-6.

There have been nice moments. Jonathan Castagna scored his first two NHL goals in Wednesday's win in San Jose. Then came a 4-1 loss to Minnesota and a one-goal loss to Chicago on Saturday, a game the Blackhawks won late after Dustin Wolf made a big save on Patrick Kane.

Our playoff odds have Calgary at 9%. What we'd watch: whether Coronato and Farabee start finishing, because there isn't much scoring elsewhere to lean on.
